questions.question: Which of these is NOT a parameter in the Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Military spending**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ease of Doing Business (EoDB)** index was an influential annual report published by the **World Bank Group** that ranked **190 economies** based on how easy it was for local firms to conduct business.
 
• The index measured business regulations across **10 specific parameters**: Starting a Business, Dealing with Construction Permits, **Getting Electricity**, Registering Property, Getting Credit, Protecting Minority Investors, **Paying Taxes**, Trading across Borders, Enforcing Contracts, and Resolving Insolvency.
 
• **Starting a business** is a core parameter that tracks the number of procedures, time, cost, and paid-in minimum capital required for a small-to-medium-sized enterprise to begin operations.
 
• **Military spending** refers to the financial resources allocated by a nation to maintain its armed forces and national security; this is a **macroeconomic/defense metric** and does not relate to the regulatory efficiency of the business environment.
 
• While the **World Bank** discontinued the **Doing Business** report in **September 2021** due to data irregularities, the parameters remain significant for studying global economic competitiveness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starting a business**:
 
 
• Focuses on the bureaucratic hurdles faced by entrepreneurs during the pre-incorporation and incorporation phases.
 
 
 
• **Getting electricity**:
 
 
• Measures the procedures, time, and cost to obtain a permanent commercial electricity connection for a newly constructed warehouse.
 
 
 
• **Paying taxes**:
 
 
• Evaluates the **Total Tax Rate**, the number of payments per year, and the hours spent complying with tax laws, including VAT and corporate income tax.
 
 
 
• The **World Bank** has introduced a new benchmarking tool called **Business Ready (B-READY)** to replace the legacy EoDB index, emphasizing **digitalization** and **sustainability**.
</ul

questions.question: What is a quicker method for resolving disagreements between businesses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alternative dispute resolution**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** refers to a collection of processes, including **mediation**, **arbitration**, and **conciliation**, that allow parties to settle disputes outside the formal **courtroom** environment.
 
• It is significantly faster than traditional **litigation** because it avoids the **procedural complexities**, **pre-trial motions**, and **congested court dockets** that often delay cases for years.
 
• In **commercial disputes**, ADR offers a flexible schedule where parties can choose their own **neutral third party** who possesses specific industry expertise, leading to more efficient and relevant outcomes.
 
• These methods focus on **collaborative problem-solving** rather than adversarial competition, which helps in reaching a resolution in a fraction of the time required for **judicial proceedings**.
 
• Settlements reached through **Arbitration** are often legally binding and enforceable under national laws like the **Arbitration and Conciliation Act**, providing the same legal security as a court order but with greater speed.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Components of ADR:**
 
 
• **Arbitration:** A formal process where an **arbitrator** hears both sides and issues a binding decision known as an **award**. It is commonly used in **international trade**.
 
• **Mediation:** A non-binding, confidential process where a **mediator** assists parties in reaching a voluntary agreement without imposing a decision.
 
• **Confidentiality:** Unlike **public trials**, ADR keeps sensitive **business data** and trade secrets private, protecting the **brand reputation** of the companies involved.
 
• **Cost-Effectiveness:** By reducing **legal billable hours** and eliminating **court fees**, ADR significantly lowers the **administrative costs** of conflict resolution.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the mandatory requirement of setting aside in liquid assets, such as gold or Government securities, by commercial banks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statutory liquidity ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** is a quantitative monetary policy tool used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** that mandates **commercial banks** to maintain a specific proportion of their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of liquid assets.

• These liquid assets must be kept in the form of **gold**, **cash**, or **unencumbered government securities** (such as **Treasury Bills** and **Dated Securities**) before the bank can offer credit to its customers.

• The primary legal authority for SLR is derived from **Section 24 (2A)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, which empowers the central bank to set and adjust this limit to ensure the **solvency** and **liquidity** of the banking system.

• By adjusting the **SLR**, the **RBI** can control the expansion of **bank credit**; an increase in **SLR** forces banks to invest more in **government securities**, thereby reducing the funds available for lending to the private sector and helping to curb **inflation**.

• Unlike the **Cash Reserve Ratio**, the assets under **SLR** are maintained by the banks themselves rather than being deposited with the **RBI**, and banks earn interest on the **securities** held under this requirement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**:

• Refers to the share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that **commercial banks** are mandated to maintain with the **RBI** strictly in the form of **liquid cash**.

• The **RBI** does not pay any **interest** on the amount maintained as **CRR**, and it serves as a primary tool to regulate **liquidity** and **money supply** in the economy.

• **Current Ratio**:

• A **liquidity ratio** that measures a company's ability to pay its **short-term obligations** or those due within one year.

• It is calculated by dividing **current assets** by **current liabilities** and is a key indicator of **financial health** for non-banking corporations.

• **Margin Requirement**:

• A qualitative **monetary policy** instrument that refers to the difference between the **market value of collateral** offered for a loan and the actual **loan amount** sanctioned.

• By increasing the **margin ratio**, the **central bank** can discourage borrowing for speculative purposes in specific sectors of the economy.

</ul

questions.question: The first Mughal Emperor to be buried outside India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur**, the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in the Indian subcontinent, was the first emperor of the dynasty to be buried outside the borders of modern-day **India**.
 
• After defeating **Ibrahim Lodi** in the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**, he established his rule in North India but died shortly after in **Agra** on **December 26, 1530**.
 
• Initially, his body was interred in the **Aram Bagh** (Garden of Rest) in **Agra**, situated on the banks of the **Yamuna River**.
 
• However, **Babur** had expressed a strong sentimental desire in his autobiography, the **Baburnama**, to be buried in his favorite city, **Kabul**, in **Afghanistan**.
 
• During the reign of either **Sher Shah Suri** or his son **Humayun** (around **1539–1544**), his remains were moved to the **Bagh-e Babur** (Gardens of Babur) in **Kabul**.
 
• His tomb is located in a **Charbagh** (four-fold garden) layout, which became a signature architectural style for future **Mughal** mausoleums.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humayun**:
 
 
• The second **Mughal** emperor is buried in **Delhi**. His tomb is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and was the first major **Mughal** structure to use red sandstone on such a large scale.
 
 
 
• **Akbar**:
 
 
• The third emperor, **Akbar the Great**, is buried in a magnificent tomb at **Sikandra**, located on the outskirts of **Agra**.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan**:
 
 
• The fifth emperor is buried in the **Taj Mahal** in **Agra**, placed next to his beloved wife, **Mumtaz Mahal**.
 
 
 
• **Other Emperors Buried Outside India**:
 
 
• **Jahangir** was buried in **Shahdara Bagh** in **Lahore**, **Pakistan**.
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, the last **Mughal** emperor, was exiled by the British and buried in **Yangon**, **Myanmar**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Mughal Emperor who abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Akbar**, the third **Mughal Emperor**, is renowned for his policies of **religious tolerance** and administrative innovations that aimed to unify a diverse Indian population.

• In **1564**, he officially abolished the **Jizya tax**, which was a per capita tax levied on non-Muslim subjects, known as **dhimmis**, living under Islamic rule.

• This significant reform was rooted in **Akbar’s** philosophy of **Sulh-i-kul** (universal peace), which sought to provide equal status to all citizens regardless of their religious beliefs.

• The abolition of **Jizya** followed his decision in **1563** to end the **Pilgrimage Tax**, a levy on Hindus visiting holy sites, further consolidating his image as a liberal and secular monarch.

• By removing these financial burdens, **Akbar** secured the loyalty of the **Rajputs** and the broader **Hindu majority**, which was essential for the expansion and stability of the **Mughal Empire**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Humayun**:

• The second **Mughal Emperor** and father of **Akbar**, whose reign was primarily defined by his struggle to reclaim the throne from the **Sur Dynasty**.

• **Jahangir**:

• The fourth **Mughal Emperor** who largely continued his father’s inclusive policies but is most noted for his patronage of **Mughal art** and his memoirs, **Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri**.

• **Shah Jahan**:

• The fifth **Mughal Emperor**, famous for the construction of the **Taj Mahal** and the **Peacock Throne**, though the status of Jizya remained unchanged during his peak years.

• **Aurangzeb**:

• The sixth **Mughal Emperor** who eventually reversed **Akbar’s** policy by re-imposing the **Jizya tax** in **1679**, leading to significant socio-political friction.

questions.question: Which Indian state is known for its traditional martial art, Gatka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gatka** is a traditional **martial art** form that originated in the **Punjab** region of India and is deeply rooted in the history of the **Sikh community**.
 
• It is essentially a style of stick-fighting that employs wooden sticks, known as **Soti**, and leather shields, called **Phari**, to simulate sword combat.
 
• The practice was formally introduced and encouraged by **Guru Hargobind Ji**, the **Sixth Sikh Guru**, who advocated for the militarization of Sikhs for self-defense and justice.
 
• It reached its peak under the **Tenth Sikh Guru**, **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, who mandated martial training for the **Khalsa** warriors in the late **17th century**.
 
• The art transitioned from a battlefield technique to a performance art and **competitive sport** during the British colonial period when the use of traditional weapons was restricted.
 
• Today, **Gatka** is an integral part of **Sikh festivals** and religious processions, especially during **Hola Mohalla** and **Vaisakhi**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigenous Sports Promotion**:
 
 
• The Government of India has officially recognized **Gatka** as a competitive sport, including it in the **Khelo India Youth Games** to preserve its cultural heritage.
 
• Other traditional martial arts promoted alongside it include **Kalaripayattu** from **Kerala**, **Thang-Ta** from **Manipur**, and **Mallakhamba** from **Madhya Pradesh** and **Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Martial Traditions**:
 
 
• **Haryana**: Predominantly famous for **Kushti** (traditional wrestling), making it a powerhouse for **Olympic** sports in India.
 
• **Rajasthan**: Known for **Shastar Vidya** and various Rajput warrior traditions involving swordsmanship and archery.
 
• **Gujarat**: While not known for a combat martial art like Gatka, it is famous for **Dandiya Raas**, which utilizes sticks for rhythmic folk dance.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In table tennis, how many consecutive serves does each player get before switching?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• Under the standard laws of **Table Tennis** established by the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**, the right to serve alternates between opponents after every **2 points** scored.

• The sequence of service remains constant throughout the game regardless of which player wins the point, ensuring each player receives an equal number of opportunities to initiate play.

• This rotation continues until the game ends or until the score reaches **10-10**, at which point the game enters a phase known as a **Deuce**.

• In a **standard match**, a game is won by the first player or pair to score **11 points**, provided there is a margin of at least **2 points** over the opponent.

• The **server** must strike the ball so that it first touches their court and then touches the receiver's court directly, passing over or around the **net assembly**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Service Exceptions and Variations**:

• **Deuce Scenarios**: When the score is tied at **10-10**, the sequence of serving and receiving remains the same, but each player shall serve for only **1 point** in turn until a lead of **2 points** is established.

• **Expedite System**: If a game is not finished after **10 minutes** of play (unless both players have scored at least 9 points), the **Expedite System** is implemented. Under this rule, service alternates after every **single point**.

• **Doubles Play**: The service rotation involves four players. The server first serves to the receiver, then the receiver becomes the server, and the partner of the initial server becomes the new receiver.

• **Service Technique**: The ball must be placed on the **open palm** of the stationary free hand and thrown at least **16 cm** into the air without imparting spin before being struck.

</ul

questions.question: The first-ever night test match in India was played in Kolkata. What colour was the cricket ball used in the game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pink**__.

• The first-ever **Day-Night Test match** in India was played at the **Eden Gardens** stadium in **Kolkata** from **November 22 to 24, 2019**.

• The match featured the national teams of **India** and **Bangladesh**, serving as the second Test of the two-match series.

• A **Pink ball** was used for the game instead of the traditional red ball to ensure optimal **visibility** for players under **floodlights** during the evening and night sessions.

• The ball was manufactured by the Indian company **SG (Sanspareils Greenlands)**, featuring a **linen-based seam** and a brighter **fluorescent finish** to counteract the visibility issues caused by the twilight sky.

• India won the historic match by an **innings and 46 runs**, with **Ishant Sharma** becoming the first Indian bowler to take a five-wicket haul with the pink ball.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Cricket Ball Varieties:**

• **Red Ball:** Used for standard **First-Class cricket** and traditional **Day Test matches**. It provides a sharp contrast against white kits but is hard to spot at night.

• **White Ball:** Specifically used in **One Day Internationals (ODIs)** and **T20 Internationals**. While highly visible under lights, it is not used in Test cricket as its color degrades significantly over 80 overs.

• **Yellow Ball:** This was briefly experimented with in early **night cricket** attempts in the late 1970s, but was ultimately rejected in favor of white and pink variations due to poor tracking against certain backgrounds.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following features are associated with the Gothic architectural style?

options.text: Pointed arches and stained glass windows

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pointed arches and stained glass windows**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Gothic architecture** is a European architectural style that flourished during the **High and Late Middle Ages**, specifically from the **12th to the 16th century**. It evolved from **Romanesque architecture** and was eventually succeeded by **Renaissance architecture**.

• The **pointed arch** (or ogival arch) is the defining characteristic of this style. Unlike the rounded arches of earlier periods, the pointed arch allowed for **greater height** and thinner walls by directing the weight of the structure more vertically.

• **Stained glass windows** were extensively used to fill large wall openings, made possible by the structural support of the arches. These windows, including the famous **rose windows**, were used to illustrate biblical stories and create a luminous, ethereal atmosphere inside **Cathedrals**.

• Other fundamental features include **ribbed vaults**, which supported heavy ceilings with a web of stone ribs, and **flying buttresses**, which were external stone supports that carried the weight of the high roofs away from the walls.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Domes and Minarets**:

• These are primary features of **Islamic architecture** and **Mughal architecture**, seen in landmarks like the **Taj Mahal** and the **Jama Masjid**.

• **Flat roofs with courtyards**:

• These are characteristic of **traditional Indian housing** and **Mediterranean architecture**, designed to improve ventilation and provide private outdoor space in warm climates.

• **Sloping tiled roofs**:

• Commonly found in **Vernacular architecture** within regions of high rainfall, such as **Kerala** or the **Konkan coast**, to facilitate efficient water drainage.

• **Historical Examples**:

• Famous Gothic structures include **Notre-Dame de Paris** in France and **Westminster Abbey** in London. In India, the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** (CSMT) is a premier example of the **Victorian Gothic Revival** style.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following ancient Indian sites is famous for its chaityas and viharas carved into rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajanta**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Ajanta Caves** are located in the **Aurangabad district** of **Maharashtra** and comprise about **30 rock-cut Buddhist monuments** excavated into a **basaltic horseshoe-shaped cliff**.

• These caves were developed in two phases, starting from the **2nd century BCE** (**Satavahana period**) and continuing to the **5th and 6th centuries CE** (**Vakataka period**).

• The site is categorized into two main types of structures: **Chaityas**, which served as **prayer halls** containing a stupa, and **Viharas**, which were **monastic residential quarters** for monks.

• The **Chaitya halls** (such as Caves 9, 10, 19, and 26) feature vaulted ceilings and polished stone, while the **Viharas** consist of central halls surrounded by sleeping cells.

• The caves are famous for their **mural paintings** and sculptures that depict scenes from the **Jataka tales** and the various lives of **Gautama Buddha**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Thanjavur**:

• Located in **Tamil Nadu**, it was the capital of the **Medieval Cholas** and is home to the **Brihadisvara Temple**, built by **Raja Raja Chola I**.

• **Mahabalipuram**:

• Situated in **Tamil Nadu**, it is known for **Pallava rock-cut architecture**, including the **Pancha Rathas** and the **Shore Temple**, but it is primarily a Hindu site.

• **Hampi**:

• Located in **Karnataka**, it served as the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** and features structural temples like the **Virupaksha Temple** and the **Stone Chariot** at **Vittala Temple**.

</ul

questions.question: The Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was initiated in the [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5808ebcaf3848af6360979d93ba863b297de423ab0546d967a6408ad032cabb2.png] Five-Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP)** was officially launched on **August 15, 1983**, which falls within the timeline of the **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985)**.

• The scheme was introduced as a **100% Centrally Funded** initiative to address the specific needs of the most marginalized section of society: the **rural landless laborers**.

• The primary mandate of the **RLEGP** was to provide a guarantee of employment for at least **100 days** in a year to at least one member of every **landless labor household**.

• Apart from direct employment, the program aimed at the creation of **durable community assets** such as **rural roads**, **social forestry**, and **minor irrigation** projects to improve the rural economy.

• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** is notable for its direct attack on **poverty** through various **target group-oriented** programs, focusing on increasing the **standard of living** and social equity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985):**

• Focus: Removal of **poverty (Garibi Hatao)**, **modernization**, and **self-reliance**.

• Significant schemes like the **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)** and **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP)** were also emphasized during this period.

• The growth target was **5.2%**, and the actual growth achieved was **5.7%**, making it a successful plan.

• **Evolution of the Programme:**

• On **April 1, 1989**, during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan**, the **RLEGP** and **NREP** were merged to form a single wage employment program called **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)**.

• The **JRY** eventually evolved through various stages into the current **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**.

questions.question: The 7th Five-Year Plan is credited with laying the foundation for which of the following major economic reform eras in India?

options.text: Economic liberalization and modernization in the 1990s

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Economic liberalization and modernization in the 1990s**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan** was implemented from **1985 to 1990** under the premiership of **Rajiv Gandhi**, shifting the economic focus toward **modernization** and **technological self-reliance**.

• It is widely credited with laying the groundwork for the **1991 Economic Reforms** by introducing concepts of **industrial liberalization** and reducing the **License Raj** constraints.

• The plan emphasized **Food, Work, and Productivity**, aiming to increase efficiency in the **private sector** while reducing the absolute dominance of the public sector.

• For the first time in Indian planning history, the **private sector** was given priority over the public sector in terms of investment outlays, creating a precursor to the **Market Economy**.

• The **Seventh Plan** achieved a remarkable **GDP growth rate of 6.01%**, significantly higher than the targeted **5.0%**, proving the efficacy of early liberalization measures.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Nationalization of banks**:

• The first major phase occurred in **1969** (14 banks) under the **Fourth Five-Year Plan**.

• The second phase took place in **1980** (6 banks) during the **Sixth Five-Year Plan**.

• **Green Revolution**:

• Launched in the mid-**1960s** (specifically **1966**) to address food shortages through **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds** and modern irrigation.

• It is primarily associated with the **Annual Plans** (Plan Holidays) and the early **Fourth Five-Year Plan**.

• **National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA)**:

• Passed in **September 2005** and renamed as **MGNREGA** in **2009**.

• This social security measure was a landmark initiative of the **Tenth Five-Year Plan** (2002−2007).

</ul

questions.question: The primary reason for the British government's decision to partition Bengal in 1905 was:

options.text: To promote the educational development of the region.
To improve the administrative efficiency of the large province.
To foster greater unity between the Hindu and Muslim populations of Bengal.
To encourage the growth of industrialization in East Bengal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To improve the administrative efficiency of the large province**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The partition of **Bengal** was officially announced on **19 July 1905** and implemented on **16 October 1905** by **Lord Curzon**, who served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905**.

• The official justification provided by the **British Government** was that the **Bengal Presidency** had become too large and populous to be managed by a single administration. It covered an area of about **189,000 square miles** with a population of nearly **78 million**.

• The restructuring divided the region into two provinces: **Western Bengal** (comprising present-day West Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha) and **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with **Dacca** (Dhaka) as the capital of the latter.

• While the stated objective was **administrative efficiency**, the real political motive was to weaken the **Indian National Movement** and create a communal divide between the **Hindu-majority** west and the **Muslim-majority** east.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Swadeshi Movement**:

• The partition led to the launch of the **Swadeshi Movement**, which emphasized the use of **indigenous products** and the boycott of British-made goods to exert economic pressure on the **Raj**.

• Prominent leaders like **Surendranath Banerjee**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, and **Lala Lajpat Rai** turned this into a mass struggle for **Swaraj** (self-rule).

• **1911 Annulment**:

• Following massive protests and rising revolutionary activities, the partition was revoked in **1911** by **Lord Hardinge** during the **Delhi Durbar**, attended by **King George V**.

• As a result, **Bihar** and **Orissa** were separated into new provinces, and the capital of **British India** was shifted from **Calcutta** to **Delhi**.

• **Communal Strategy**:

• The British successfully encouraged the formation of the **All-India Muslim League** in **1906** at **Dacca**, capitalizing on the political division to foster a separate identity for the Muslim elite.

</ul

questions.question:
The "Indian Independence Act of 1947" outlined the terms for the transfer of power and the creation of independent India and Pakistan.

Which of the following was a key provision of this Act regarding the princely states?

options.text: It mandated the immediate integration of all princely states into either India or Pakistan based on geographical contiguity.
It granted the princely states the freedom to choose whether to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
It stipulated that the British government would continue to exercise paramountcy over the princely states.
It ensured that the revenue sharing agreements between the princely states and the new dominions would remain unchanged.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It granted the princely states the freedom to choose whether to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Independence Act of 1947** was a landmark legislation passed by the **British Parliament** that set the date for the partition of British India into two sovereign dominions: **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• A primary provision regarding the **princely states** was the termination of **British Paramountcy**. This meant that all treaties, agreements, and obligations between the **British Crown** and the rulers of these states lapsed on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• The Act did not mandate the integration of states based on geography; instead, it legally provided the **562 princely states** with the choice to accede to either of the two new dominions or to remain **independent**.
 
• This legal framework meant that the states were no longer under the **suzerainty** of the British monarch and were technically restored to the status they held before their treaties with the British.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integration Process**:
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, the first Home Minister of India, and **V.P. Menon** played a monumental role in the political integration of these states.
 
• The **Instrument of Accession** was the legal document through which rulers agreed to join India, typically surrendering powers over **Defense**, **External Affairs**, and **Communications**.
 
 
 
• **The Mountbatten Plan**:
 
 
• The Act was based on the **June 3 Plan** proposed by **Lord Mountbatten**, the last Viceroy of India, which aimed to resolve the communal deadlock between the **Indian National Congress** and the **Muslim League**.
 
 
 
• **Lapse of Treaties**:
 
 
• The Act explicitly stated that all **commercial and financial agreements** between the Crown and the states would also expire, necessitating the creation of **Standstill Agreements** to maintain administrative continuity.
 
 
 
• **Exceptional Cases**:
 
 
• While most states joined one of the dominions by August 1947, states like **Hyderabad**, **Junagadh**, and **Jammu and Kashmir** initially hesitated or sought independence, leading to further political and military interventions.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
The "Wood's Despatch" of 1854 recommended several significant changes in the Indian education system.

Which of the following was a key recommendation of this despatch?

options.text: The immediate vernacularization of all levels of education.
The establishment of a comprehensive system of education from the primary to the university level, with English as the medium of instruction at higher levels.
The complete privatization of the education sector in India.
The exclusive focus on the training of religious leaders and scholars.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The establishment of a comprehensive system of education from the primary to the university level, with English as the medium of instruction at higher levels.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wood's Despatch** of **1854** is famously known as the **Magna Carta of English Education in India**, as it was the first document to provide a comprehensive plan for the spread of education.
 
• Prepared by **Sir Charles Wood**, the then President of the **Board of Control**, the despatch was addressed to **Lord Dalhousie**, the Governor-General of India.
 
• It proposed a **structured educational hierarchy** consisting of **Primary Schools** at the bottom, followed by **Middle Schools**, **High Schools**, **Colleges**, and **Universities**.
 
• The despatch recommended that **English** be the medium of instruction for **higher education** (University level) while **vernacular languages** (local mother tongues) be used at the **school level** to ensure wider reach.
 
• It advised the establishment of **Universities** in the presidency towns of **Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras**, modeled after the **University of London**, to regulate and conduct examinations.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Framework**:
 
 
• It recommended the creation of a **Department of Public Instruction (DPI)** in every province to supervise educational activities and maintain standards.
 
 
 
• **Financial Support and Privatization**:
 
 
• To encourage **private enterprise**, the despatch introduced the **Grant-in-Aid system** for private schools that provided **secular education** and met government standards.
 
 
 
• **Social Initiatives**:
 
 
• The document placed significant emphasis on **Women's Education** and **Vocational Training**, advocating for the establishment of **Normal Schools** to train professional teachers.
 
 
 
• **Secular Focus**:
 
 
• It mandated that education in **government-aided institutions** must remain strictly **secular**, although private institutions were allowed to include religious instruction.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What was the theme of India's Republic Day Parade 2025?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which dance form in Manipur involves the use of swords, spears, and shields?

questions.question:
With reference to Copper production in India, consider the following statements:

1. India has turned into a net importer of refined copper in recent times.

2. Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Jharkhand are the only states involved in the production of copper in the country.

3. During the copper smelting process, the sulfur dioxide and particulate matter are predominantly released into the atmosphere.

Which of the statements given above is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Historically, India was a net exporter of copper; however, since the **financial year 2018-19**, the country has become a **net importer** of refined copper. This shift was primarily triggered by the permanent closure of the **Sterlite Copper plant** in **Tuticorin**, Tamil Nadu, which accounted for nearly **40 percent** of India's smelting capacity. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• While **Madhya Pradesh** (Malanjkhand belt), **Rajasthan** (Khetri and Alwar belts), and **Jharkhand** (Singhbhum belt) are the primary producers contributing the bulk of India's copper, they are not the only states involved. Copper deposits and minor production activities are also documented in states like **Karnataka**, **Andhra Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Sikkim**. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**
 
• Copper is extracted from **sulfide ores** through the **smelting process**, which involves heating the concentrate. This thermal extraction releases significant volumes of **sulfur dioxide (SO₂)** gas and **particulate matter (PM)**. If not captured by **scrubbers** or converted into **sulfuric acid**, these pollutants contribute to **acid rain** and respiratory hazards. **Hence, statement 3 is correct.**

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Copper Deposits:**
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:** The **Malanjkhand** mine in **Balaghat** district is the largest open-pit copper mine in India.
 
• **Rajasthan:** The **Khetri** copper belt in **Jhunjhunu** is a major historical and functional mining site managed by **Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL)**.
 
• **Jharkhand:** The **Singhbhum** district is known for the **Mosabani** and **Rakha** mines.
 
 
 
• **Properties and Uses:**
 
 
• Copper is a **ductile**, **malleable**, and **excellent conductor** of electricity and heat.
 
• It is indispensable in the **electrical industry** for making wires, **transformers**, and **motors**.
 
• It is also used to create **alloys** such as **brass** (copper and zinc) and **bronze** (copper and tin).
 
 
 
• **Smelting Byproducts:**
 
 
• Beyond air pollutants, copper smelting produces **iron silicate slag**, which is used in **cement manufacturing** and road construction.
 
• Captured **sulfur dioxide** is frequently utilized to produce **sulfuric acid**, making copper plants a major source of this industrial chemical.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Chota Nagpur plateau region receives the majority of its rainfall through which of the following wind system?

options.text: Arabian Sea branch of South-West monsoon winds
Bay of Bengal branch of South-West monsoon winds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabian Sea branch of South-West monsoon winds**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chota Nagpur plateau**, spanning across **Jharkhand**, **Odisha**, and **West Bengal**, acts as a significant barrier and recipient for monsoon winds in eastern India.
 
• During the **South-West monsoon** season (June to September), the **Arabian Sea branch** of the monsoon winds enters the Indian landmass and moves towards the north-eastern part of the peninsula.
 
• A specific part of the **Arabian Sea branch** moves through the **Narmada** and **Tapi** river valleys, crossing the **Maikal Range** and entering the **Chota Nagpur plateau**.
 
• Although the plateau receives moisture from both branches, the **Arabian Sea branch** is often credited with providing a substantial and consistent portion of the rainfall to this region due to its direct inland trajectory.
 
• The **orographic** features of the plateau, including hills like the **Parasnath**, force these moisture-laden winds to rise, resulting in heavy precipitation that sustains the region's **deciduous forests**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal branch of South-West monsoon winds**:
 
 
• This branch initially moves towards **Myanmar** and **Bangladesh** before being deflected by the **Himalayan mountains**.
 
• It moves westward along the **Indo-Gangetic plains** and contributes significantly to the rainfall in **North-East India** and the **Gangetic belt**.
 
 
 
• **North-Eastern monsoon winds**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Retreating Monsoon**, these winds blow from the land to the sea during **October and November**.
 
• They pick up moisture over the **Bay of Bengal** and primarily cause rainfall along the **Coromandel Coast** of **Tamil Nadu** and **Andhra Pradesh**, leaving the plateau region mostly dry.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the 2015 India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (LBA):

1) As per the 2015 agreement, 51 Bangladeshi enclaves in India and 111 Indian enclaves in Bangladesh were exchanged.

2) A majority of enclave residents from Bangladesh opted to retain Bangladeshi citizenship after the transfer.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 is Correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2015 Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)** was a historic treaty between **India** and **Bangladesh** that facilitated the transfer of **111 Indian enclaves** (adversely held territories) located in Bangladesh and **51 Bangladeshi enclaves** located in India. This exchange involved roughly **17,160 acres** of land transferred to Bangladesh and **7,110 acres** of land transferred to India. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• Following the transfer of sovereignty on **July 31, 2015**, residents of the enclaves were granted the right to choose their citizenship. According to the joint survey conducted by both nations, the vast majority of the residents in the **51 Bangladeshi enclaves** within India opted for **Indian citizenship**. Conversely, the majority of residents in the **111 Indian enclaves** within Bangladesh chose to remain there and accept **Bangladeshi citizenship**. Only **979 individuals** from the Indian enclaves in Bangladesh opted to move to the Indian mainland to retain their original citizenship. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The exchange was operationalized through the **100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015** of the Indian Constitution, which amended the **First Schedule** to redefine the boundaries of **Assam**, **West Bengal**, **Meghalaya**, and **Tripura**.
 
 
• **Historical Context**: The issue of **Chhitmahals** (enclaves) originated from the flawed **Radcliffe Award** of **1947**. Previous attempts to resolve it included the **Nehru-Noon Agreement** of **1958** and the **Indira-Mujib Accord** of **1974**.
 
• **Humanitarian Impact**: Before the **2015 LBA**, enclave residents were effectively stateless, lacking access to basic services like **healthcare**, **education**, and **legal protection** because officials from their parent country could not reach them.
 
• **Border Demarcation**: Besides the enclaves, the agreement also settled **6.1 kilometers** of **un-demarcated border** and addressed the issue of **Adverse Possessions**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: As per Census 2011, what was the population density of India?

questions.question: The NISAR satellite mission is primarily related to which type of imaging?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radar imaging**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **NISAR** is an acronym for **NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar**, representing a high-profile joint collaboration between the **United States (NASA)** and **India (ISRO)**.

• The mission is specifically designed to perform **radar imaging** using a **dual-frequency** system consisting of **L-band** and **S-band** Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) instruments.

• The primary scientific objective is to observe and measure **Earth’s dynamic surfaces**, including changes in **ice sheets**, **forest biomass**, and **land deformation** caused by earthquakes or volcanoes.

• Unlike optical sensors, **SAR** technology allows the satellite to capture data with high precision regardless of **weather conditions**, cloud cover, or the absence of sunlight (day or night).

• The satellite is scheduled to be launched into a **Sun-synchronous orbit** and will map the entire global land and ice masses every **12 days** to provide consistent time-series data.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)**:

• This is an **active sensing** technique where the satellite transmits its own microwave signals and records the reflection to create **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** images of the surface.

• The **L-band** (provided by NASA) has a wavelength of approximately **24 cm**, which is ideal for penetrating dense foliage and measuring ground movement.

• The **S-band** (provided by ISRO) has a wavelength of about **12 cm** and is useful for monitoring light vegetation and heavy weather conditions.

• **Optical Imaging**:

• Requires **visible light** to function; hence, it is ineffective during the night and cannot see through **clouds** or **thick smoke**.

• **Spectroscopy**:

• Involves analyzing the **chemical composition** and physical properties of matter by studying its interaction with the electromagnetic spectrum, often used in **hyperspectral imaging** missions like **HysIS**.

• **Sample Return**:

• Refers to missions that physically collect material from extra-terrestrial bodies and return it to Earth, such as the **OSIRIS-REx** or **Hayabusa** missions.

__
 
• **Reusable Launch Vehicles (RLVs)** are engineered with the specific goal of recovering the **launch vehicle stages** for multiple missions. questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a nitrogenous base in DNA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uracil**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Deoxyribonucleic Acid** (**DNA**) is composed of four **nitrogenous bases** that carry genetic information: **Adenine** (A), **Guanine** (G), **Cytosine** (C), and **Thymine** (T).

• **Uracil** (U) is a **nitrogenous base** that is specifically found in **Ribonucleic Acid** (**RNA**) and is not a component of **DNA** under normal biological conditions.

• In the **double-helix** structure of **DNA**, **Adenine** pairs with **Thymine** via two **hydrogen bonds**, while **Guanine** pairs with **Cytosine** via three **hydrogen bonds**.

• The absence of **Uracil** in **DNA** and its presence in **RNA** is a key distinguishing factor between these two types of **nucleic acids**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Nitrogenous Base Classification**:

• **Purines**: These consist of **Adenine** and **Guanine**, which have a **double-ring structure** (a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring).

• **Pyrimidines**: These include **Cytosine**, **Thymine** (in **DNA**), and **Uracil** (in **RNA**), which possess a **single six-membered ring** structure.

• **Structural Comparison**:

• **Thymine** is chemically known as **5-methyluracil**. The primary structural difference is that **Thymine** has a **methyl group** at the C5 position, whereas **Uracil** lacks this group.

• The use of **Thymine** in **DNA** instead of **Uracil** provides greater **stability** and prevents errors during **DNA replication** by allowing repair enzymes to identify deaminated **Cytosine**.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is now explicitly considered a 'document' under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A server log file**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**, which replaced the **Indian Evidence Act of 1872**, has significantly expanded the legal definition of a **document** to encompass the digital age.
 
• Under **Section 2(1)(d)** of the Act, a **document** is defined as any matter expressed, described, or inscribed upon any substance by means of letters, figures, or marks, intended for recording that matter.
 
• The Act explicitly includes **electronic and digital records** within this definition, specifically mentioning **server logs**, **emails**, **documents on computers**, **laptop or smartphone messages**, and **websites**.
 
• By including a **server log file**, the law recognizes automated digital footprints as valid evidence, allowing for better prosecution of **cyber-crimes** and technology-related disputes.
 
• This shift ensures that **electronic records** are treated with the same legal weight as traditional paper-based evidence, provided their **integrity** is maintained.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**:
 
 
• The Act received the **President's assent** on **December 25, 2023**, and came into effect on **July 1, 2024**.
 
• It introduces provisions for the **admissibility of electronic evidence** as primary evidence under **Section 61**, provided the storage remains in its original digital form.
 
• **Section 63** of the BSA outlines the requirements for a **certificate** to authenticate electronic records, replacing the older **Section 65B** of the previous Act.
 
• Other digital formats recognized include **locational evidence**, **voice mail messages**, and data retrieved from **cloud storage** or **digital devices**.
 
 
 
• **Excluded Concepts**:
 
 
• **Verbal agreements** are considered oral evidence rather than documentary evidence unless reduced to writing or a digital record.
 
• **Spontaneous thoughts** are intangible and do not meet the criteria of being recorded on a substance or medium to qualify as a document.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Urea Subsidy Scheme:

Statement 1: Urea is sold to farmers at a fixed Maximum Retail Price (MRP).

Statement 2: The subsidy is directly transferred to the bank accounts of farmers.

Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urea** is the only fertilizer in India that remains under statutory price control. The **Government of India** fixes a uniform **Maximum Retail Price (MRP)** for urea across the country, ensuring it remains affordable for the farming community. The current MRP is approximately **Rs 242 per 45 kg bag** (excluding taxes and neem coating charges). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Under the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** system for fertilizers, the subsidy is not paid directly to the farmers' bank accounts. Instead, the **Government of India** pays the subsidy amount directly to the **fertilizer companies** (manufacturers or importers) after the actual sale is made to the farmer through a **Point of Sale (PoS)** device. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Urea Subsidy** is the difference between the **cost of production** (for domestic units) or the **Import Parity Price (IPP)** (for imported urea) and the fixed **MRP** paid by the farmers. This entire fiscal burden is borne by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neem Coated Urea (NCU):**
 
 
• In **2015**, the government made it mandatory for all domestic producers to produce **100% Neem Coated Urea**.
 
• This initiative was launched to prevent the **illegal diversion** of highly subsidized urea for industrial uses and to improve **Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE)**.
 
 
 
• **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme:**
 
 
• Unlike urea, Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilizers like **DAP** and **MOP** are governed by the **NBS Scheme** launched in **April 2010**.
 
• Under **NBS**, a fixed amount of subsidy is provided based on the nutrient content (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potash, and Sulphur) rather than a fixed retail price.
 
 
 
• **New Urea Policy (NUP) 2015:**
 
 
• The **NUP 2015** was implemented to maximize indigenous production, promote **energy efficiency** in urea plants, and rationalize the total subsidy burden.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)?

options.text: Promoting cultivation of a tropical oil-rich crop

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promoting cultivation of a tropical oil-rich crop**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)** is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** launched by the Government of India in **August 2021** to transform the edible oil sector.

• The primary objective of this mission is to significantly increase the domestic production of **Crude Palm Oil (CPO)** by promoting the cultivation of **Oil Palm**, which is a highly productive **tropical oil-rich crop**.

• The mission targets expanding the area under oil palm cultivation to **10 lakh hectares** by **2025-26** and further to **16.7 lakh hectares** by **2029-30**, focusing heavily on the **North-Eastern states** and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.

• With a total financial outlay of **Rs. 11,040 crore**, the initiative aims to reduce India's heavy reliance on edible oil imports, which currently account for nearly **60%** of the total domestic consumption.

• The scheme provides **financial assistance** to farmers for planting material and maintenance, while also establishing a **Viability Price** mechanism to protect farmers from the volatility of international CPO prices.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Oil Palm Characteristics:**

• It is a perennial **tropical crop** that yields much higher quantities of oil per unit of land compared to traditional oilseeds like **mustard**, **groundnut**, or **soybean**.

• A single hectare of oil palm can produce approximately **4 tonnes of oil**, which is about **10 to 46 times** more productive than other oilseed crops.

• **Economic Significance:**

• India is the **world's largest importer** of edible oils, spending a massive amount of foreign exchange annually on imports primarily from **Indonesia** and **Malaysia**.

• The mission is a key component of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) initiative, aiming to achieve self-sufficiency in **vegetable oils** and enhance the income of **Indian farmers**.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why indirect taxes are considered regressive?

options.text: They apply only to the wealthy
They impact all income groups equally

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They impact all income groups equally**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect taxes**, such as **GST**, **Value Added Tax (VAT)**, and **Excise Duty**, are levied on the sale of goods and services rather than on an individual's earnings.
 
• These taxes are considered **regressive** because the tax rate is fixed for a specific product or service, meaning **all income groups** pay the exact same amount of tax for the same purchase.
 
• While the nominal tax amount is identical, the **relative burden** is significantly higher for **low-income individuals**. For instance, a 100-rupee tax on a luxury item represents a much larger percentage of a poor person's daily wage than that of a wealthy individual.
 
• Because **lower-income households** tend to spend a higher proportion of their total income on **essential consumption**, they end up contributing a larger share of their earnings toward indirect taxes compared to high-income earners.
 
• The **incidence of tax** is shifted from the manufacturer or service provider to the final **consumer**, regardless of the consumer's financial capacity or **wealth status**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Progressive Tax**:
 
 
• Unlike indirect taxes, **Direct Taxes** like **Income Tax** are typically **progressive**.
 
• In this system, the **tax rate increases** as the taxpayer's **taxable income** increases, ensuring that those with higher financial capacity contribute more to the **exchequer**.
 
 
 
• **Proportional Tax**:
 
 
• Also known as a **Flat Tax**, where the tax rate remains constant regardless of the income level or the size of the **tax base**.
 
 
 
• **Tax Equity**:
 
 
• **Vertical Equity** suggests that people with a greater ability to pay should pay more tax, a principle often violated by the **uniform nature** of indirect taxation.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: When is total revenue maximized in relation to elasticity?

options.text: When elasticity is greater than one
When elasticity is less than one
When marginal cost equals marginal revenue

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When elasticity equals one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Total Revenue (TR)** is the total amount of money a firm receives from selling its goods or services, calculated as **Price (P) × Quantity (Q)**.
 
• **Price Elasticity of Demand (PED)** measures the responsiveness of the quantity demanded of a good to a change in its price. When the **absolute value of elasticity** is exactly **1**, it is known as **Unitary Elasticity**.
 
• The relationship between **Marginal Revenue (MR)** and elasticity is expressed by the formula: **MR = P × (1 − 1/|e|)**. When elasticity **|e| = 1**, the **Marginal Revenue** becomes **zero**.
 
• In calculus, the maximum point of a function (Total Revenue) occurs when its first derivative (Marginal Revenue) is **zero**. Therefore, **Total Revenue** reaches its peak at the point where the demand curve is **unit elastic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When elasticity is greater than one (Elastic Demand):**
 
 
• A decrease in price leads to a proportionately larger increase in quantity demanded, causing **Total Revenue** to rise.
 
• In this range, **Marginal Revenue** is **positive**.
 
 
 
• **When elasticity is less than one (Inelastic Demand):**
 
 
• A decrease in price leads to a proportionately smaller increase in quantity demanded, causing **Total Revenue** to fall.
 
• In this range, **Marginal Revenue** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **When marginal cost equals marginal revenue:**
 
 
• This is the condition for **Profit Maximization** rather than **Revenue Maximization**.
 
• A **Rational Producer** aims to produce at the level where the additional cost of the last unit equals the additional revenue gained, ensuring the highest net profit.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Usha Mehta is famously known for which of the following contributions during the Quit India Movement?

options.text: Leading armed struggle against British forces
Organizing the underground radio to broadcast nationalist messages
Being the first woman to be executed by the British for revolutionary activities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Organizing the underground radio to broadcast nationalist messages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Usha Mehta** was a dedicated freedom fighter who gained national prominence during the **Quit India Movement** in **1942** for establishing the **Secret Congress Radio**, also known as **Azad Hindi Radio**. Hence, the statement about organizing the underground radio is correct.
 
• The underground station began its first broadcast on **August 14, 1942**, helping to spread the message of **Mahatma Gandhi** and other leaders after the **British Raj** arrested the top Congress leadership under **Operation Zero Hour**. Hence, her contribution was vital for maintaining communication among activists.
 
• To avoid detection by the **British authorities**, the radio transmitter was frequently moved between different hidden locations across **Bombay** (now Mumbai). The station operated on a frequency of **42.34 meters** and successfully bypassed strict colonial censorship for nearly three months. Hence, this clandestine activity provided a platform for uncensored nationalist news.
 
• **Usha Mehta** and her team, which included **Vithalbhai Jhaveri**, **Chandrakant Jhaveri**, and **Babubhai Thakkar**, were eventually betrayed and arrested by the police on **November 12, 1942**. Hence, her courageous efforts concluded with a period of rigorous imprisonment in **Yerawada Jail**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolutionary and Protest Contexts**:
 
 
• **Armed Struggle**: While groups like the **Indian National Army (INA)** led by **Subhas Chandra Bose** and the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** engaged in armed conflict, **Usha Mehta's** role was focused on non-violent but clandestine communication.
 
• **Execution of Women**: **Matangini Hazra** was a notable martyr of the **Quit India Movement** who was shot dead by British police while leading a procession, whereas **Pritilata Waddedar** is remembered for her revolutionary sacrifice during the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** of **1932**.
 
• **Mass Protests in Bombay**: **Aruna Asaf Ali** is the leader most famously associated with leading mass protests and hoisting the **Indian National Flag** at the **Gowalia Tank Maidan** in **Bombay** on **August 9, 1942**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Recognition**:
 
 
• Following India's independence, **Usha Mehta** became a distinguished academic and was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1998** for her exceptional service to the nation.
 
 
</ul
